why: only use ayodhya.300 'कृपा अनुग्रहु अंगु अघाई' — Gita Press reads it as 'साङ्गोपाङ्ग' (in every part, fully), not 'पक्ष / acceptance'; other commentators take अंगु = अंगीकार. Sense unsettled

r 'अनीप' is not a standard Sanskrit word; Gita Press takes अनिप as 'सेनापति' (cf. Skt अनीकप / अनीकिनीपति), but lanka.46 may also read it as a proper name alongside अकंपन, अतिकाय. Root and whether it is a name unsettled
r 'आयसु' is just the variant form, while आयसु itself has r 'आज्ञा' (a synonym); etymologically आयसु < Skt आदेश. Unsure which root convention the dictionary wants
glossed 'ढेले / ऊबड़-खाबड़पन' (clods), but Gita Press (ayodhya.311 'कुस कंटक काँकरीं कुराईं') renders it 'दरारें' (cracks/ruts). Could not settle which
sense 'अकेले' is right (aranya.24, Gita Press), but r 'अकेला' is doubtful: अकसर is usually derived from एक + सर, not from अकेला
sense 'डाह' (सौतियाडाह) is right; r 'ईर्ष्या' as the source of आरेस is uncertain
ayodhya.269 'देवँ दीन्ह सबु मोहि अभारू' — Gita Press 'सारा भार'; unclear whether अभारू = भार (r भार) or अ + भार / a variant; r left as is

Gita Press reads 'भरत भगति सब कै मति जंत्री' as 'बुद्धिको कील दिया' (a verb: bound/spellbound), while the entry gives a noun 'नियंत्रक / controller'. Both readings are defended by commentators; please decide.
Entry glosses 'छरहरे / slender'; Gita Press renders 'छरे छबीले छयल' as 'चुने हुए' (select, picked). Unsure which sense is intended.
Fixed meaning to 'destroy(er)' per Gita Press, but the Sanskrit root is ambiguous (jahi is imperative of both हन् 'kill' and हा 'abandon'); root left blank.
Postposition 'से बढ़कर/than'; root given as 'अपेक्षा', which is a gloss rather than a source form. Unsure of the correct etymon.
Meaning 'दावानल / forest fire' fits, but r 'दावाग्नि' is a synonym, not the etymon (likely from दग्ध / डाढ़ना).
Glossed 'आनंद / उत्साह' with r 'चैन'; Gita Press gives 'चाव (उत्साह)'. Whether चेन derives from चैन is doubtful.
Entry (and ग, घ, ङ, च, छ) describe the letter used as a doha sub-numbering marker (e.g. ३ (ख)); fine if such tokens should be in the dictionary at all.
Sense 'leapt' is right, but root given as तड़कना (to crack); likely तरकना (Awadhi 'to leap'); not certain.
Sense 'swift-flowing' matches Gita Press (तेज धारा), but root 'तुरावती' looks invented; may be from तोड़ना (bank-breaking) or त्वरा; unverified.
lanka 67 'निसाचर दर्पा' is rendered by Gita Press as 'गर्वित हुआ' (a verb, past); entry treats it as adjective 'घमंड से भरा' with root दर्प; unsure whether to relabel as verb.
'साइँ दोहाईं' (ayodhya 298): Gita Press reads it as स्वामि-द्रोह (traitor to the master), so root should be द्रोह not दुहाई; but it can also be read as 'दुहाई' (I swear by the lord). Unsettled.
Sense 'wait for' is right (Gita Press: प्रतीक्षा करना), but root given as परखना (to test); the 'wait' verb is usually cited as परिखना/परेखना. Same issue in परिखेहु.
Same as परिखेसु: meaning 'wait' correct, root परखना questionable.
'सुनि कपि बचन बिहसि बिहरावा' (sundar.22): sense 'laughed it off' is fine, but root बहलाना is doubtful; possibly बिहराना/बहराना (to dismiss, divert)
'करहिं कहत न बागहीं' (lanka.90): root given as बकना; the Awadhi verb is probably बागना (to babble/boast); could not confirm from Gita Press gloss (truncated)

hi 'बरसाते हुए' (transitive) with r बरसना (intransitive); same mismatch in बरषहिं, बरषहीं, बरषि, बरषे, बरिसहिं, बरिसा, बरिसि. Awadhi बरषना is used both ways; decide on one convention (r बरसना with both senses, or बरसाना for transitive uses)
root पल्लवना is rare/archaic; may be better as पलुहना or 'पल्लवित होना'
'सेवत बिषय बिबर्ध' = increases (verb); root given as adjective विवर्धित; a verb root (बिबर्धना / वर्धना) may be preferable
r 'वदना' is not a Hindi verb; Sanskrit present participle of वद् or Awadhi बदना; sibling बदत uses बदना
hi 'राक्षस' for पिशाच; Gita Press often renders loosely, but pishacha and rakshasa are distinct beings; same for पिसाचिनि ('राक्षसियाँ')
'मागध सूत बिदुष बंदीजन' (bal.309): glossed 'विदूषक / विद्वान' with r विदूषक; could mean learned men (विदुष) rather than jesters; context does not settle it
root 'बलवंड' is not a standard word; likely from बलिवंड/बरिबंड (mighty); left as is
Sanskrit पश्यामि is present 'I see', but hi gives 'देखूँगी' first and is feminine-only; in lanka.107 the speaker is Sita (so feminine fits that verse) — consider 'देखता/देखती हूँ'
'ऊँट बिसराते' glossed 'खच्चर' with r बेसरा; plausible (बेसर = mule) but the -ते ending is unusual; not verified
Only use 'चहत न भरत भूपतहि भोरें' means kingship (Gita Press: राजपद), as hi/en say; but r is भूपति (king). The base may be भूपत/भूपतित्व; unsure which root to give

'मोह मन मापा' = mind stupefied; r मापना here is the homograph 'to become intoxicated' (Shabdasagar), not 'to measure', but g says विशेषण for a past verb form; may confuse the reader, unsure whether to relabel
same as मापा ('माजहि खाइ मीन जनु मापी'): past fem. of मापना 'become stupefied', labelled विशेषण; root homograph of 'measure'
'गहि पद पटकेउ भूमि भवाँई' = whirling him round; r given as घुमाना (a synonym) — the Awadhi/Hindi verb is भँवाना; left as is since घुमाना is the Hindi infinitive equivalent
'राजु कि भूँजब भरत' = will Bharata enjoy the kingdom; r भोगना is the synonym, the Awadhi verb is भूँजना (from Skt भुज्), which in Hindi means 'roast'; unsure which root the owner wants
sense 'सुख / joy' fits all uses, but r 'सच' (truth) looks like a false etymology; correct source form (Skt. शर्म? सच्च?) not settled
'सामग्री' fits ayodhya.187, but r 'सामान' (Persian) is doubtful as the source of Awadhi समाऊ; possibly from समाज/सामग्री
may be सु + बानि (good habit/nature) rather than सु + वाणी: ayodhya.299 'राउरि रीति सुबानि' reads as 'good nature'; entry gives only 'सुंदर वाणी वाली'
bal.91 'सुघरी सोचाई' = had (the hour) fixed/checked (शोधवाकर); r 'शोधना' is non-causative and the form may be causative of सोचना or सोधना
Gita Press 'नष्ट करके'; r 'हटाना' is a synonym; the verb may be हाँतना (to set aside, destroy)
meaning 'होड़' correct (bal.69), but r 'स्पर्धा' is a synonym; Awadhi हिसिषा may derive from ईर्ष्या
'रोककर' (bal.319 नयन नीरु हटि) is transitive, but r हटना is intransitive; root may be हटकना/हटाना
bal.333 Gita Press renders as 'सुन्दर शय्याएँ' (fine beds); entry 'अच्छी वस्तुएँ' may be too vague or wrong
ayodhya.232 'सगुनु खीरु' glossed 'गुण' by Gita Press; r 'सगुण' (with attributes) may be wrong if the word is स+गुन 'merit'
r 'सशंकना' is not a standard Hindi verb; perhaps सशंकित होना / संकना
Sanskrit singular inside bahuvrīhi (कंज लोचनं = lotus-eyed); hi/en 'नेत्र / eyes' does not convey the adjectival compound role
'धारण करके / assuming' fits bal.152 only (Gita Press 'सजकर'); unsure whether a more general 'सजाकर, सँवारकर' should replace it
In 'कुशल पंडिताही रुसो' unclear whether पंडिता is feminine 'woman scholar' (following विदुषी स्त्रिया) or plural/oblique of पंडित 'scholars'; entry assumes feminine.
Part 'रंग = रमण करनेवाला (प्रभु)' is questionable; रंग usually 'stage/arena' or from रञ्ज् 'delight'. Etymology needs a source.
Identification as the poet of the Namaskārāṣṭaka naming himself is unverified; could be an epithet ('king of enchanters').
Labelled noun in dative; सार्थक is an adjective, and in 'नरा सार्थका साधनीभूत' it may qualify नरा or mean 'for fulfilment'. Analysis uncertain.
r 'माय' given; could equally be poetic मा 'mother' in its own right; also Sanskrit prohibitive मा 'do not' is a common sense of this form not mentioned.
r 'तू' while sibling forms तुझी/तुझें use 'तुझा'; consider making roots consistent.

r gives 'अनुपम'. Tulsī's अनूप (अनूप रूप भूपतिं) is a tadbhava of अनुपम, but in Sanskrit lexicons अनूप is a separate word meaning 'watery/marshy land'. Decide whether r should say 'अनुपम (तद्भव)' or be dropped.

r 'हरतोषण' cannot produce the dative -तोषये (that would be -तोषणाय). The form points to an irregular i-stem (हर + तोषि, from तुष्), used as तोषाय/तुष्टये. The root needs correcting, but I am not sure of the citation form to use.

In Rāma Rakṣā 38 (रमे रामे मनोरमे … वरानने) मनोरमे is often taken as a vocative to Pārvatī ('O lovely one'), not a locative agreeing with रामे as the entry has it. Also p gives [रमे, रमानेवाले], but the part should be रम.

Glossed 'born of Brahmā's line' for Śiva (Araṇya maṅgalācaraṇa 1). Commentators differ (e.g. Brahmā's offspring as Rudra vs. 'one devoted to the Brahmin race'); I could not confirm which reading the site follows.

The र् implies मुनिः + ध्यानगम्यम्, or a misprint for the compound मुनिध्यानगम्यम्. The entry analyses it as a compound (मुनि + ध्यान + गम्य), which matches the meaning but not the sandhi of the text as printed.

g 'अव्ययीभाव'. In भजे सशक्ति सानुजं it works as an adjective (bahuvrīhi, Tulsī's form for सशक्तिम्) qualifying the Lord, like सानुजं beside it. The label may be wrong, but Tulsī's irregular Sanskrit makes this uncertain.

In त्रातु सदा नो कृपा वरूथः it is glossed 'समूह / राशि' (mass). In Sanskrit वरूथ primarily means armour/shield/protection, which may be the intended sense ('shield of grace'). Gita Press-style glosses give 'कृपाके पुंज', so I left it.

कामप्रेः is glossed 'पूर्णकाम के'. In the Aitareya passage, interpreters take kāmapri either as 'one whose desires are fulfilled' or as 'fulfiller of desires' (an epithet of Marutta). I could not settle it.

TS pada is गोघ्ने (ए→अ before उत). That is either dat. sg. of गोहन् (agreeing with ते ... क्षयद्वीराय) or loc. sg. of गोघ्न; the entry gives a nominative 'cow-slaying (form)' and no case. Need Sāyaṇa's reading to set r/g
Same as गोघ्न: dat. of पूरुषहन् or loc. of पूरुषघ्न, but glossed as a nominative ('that slays men') with r पूरुषघ्न
hi says 'कर्मका फल', p says 'ऋत, सत्कर्म'. Sāyaṇa may read ऋतम् = यज्ञादि कर्म and अमृतम् = its fruit (heaven); the meanings file also says 'fruit'. Check Sāyaṇa on TS 4.7.3
Glossed 'good grain'; the prefix कु- suggests 'poor/inferior barley', which may be Sāyaṇa's reading. Check TS 4.7.4
वस्यस् is a comparative 'better, welfare' (beside श्रेयः); 'उत्तम निवास / a good home' looks like an etymology from वस् 'dwell'. Check Sāyaṇa
Glossed copper and लोहम् bronze. In Vedic usage श्याम(अयस्) is often iron and लोह copper, so the two may be swapped. Check Sāyaṇa on TS 4.7.5
See श्यामञ्च: लोह may be copper (lohāyasa), not bronze
work.json reads दिष्णिया-; TS has धिष्णियाः. The key (and verse text) is probably a typo for धिष्णियाश्च; the entry glosses it as धिष्ण्याः
Surface अस्सद्भ्यो looks like a source typo for अस्यद्भ्यो (TS नमोऽस्यद्भ्यः); the part gloss already says अस्यद्भ्यः
Surface विद्यद्भ्यः looks like a source typo for विध्यद्भ्यः (√व्यध्); the part already says विध्यद्भ्यः
Text reads मृत्युर्मे पाहि; the usual reading is मृत्योर्मा पाहि. The parts give मृत्योः + मे, but पाहि needs accusative मा, and मृत्युर् is not मृत्योः. Probably a source variant or corruption
अरः glossed 'नष्ट करो'. The sense of मा अरः/आरः (√ऋ 'harm, afflict'?) and how the elision mark is to be read need Sāyaṇa
Glossed as present 'we worship' with no g. The form looks like an s-aorist subjunctive/imperative-type Vedic form ('let us worship'); grammar not settled
RV 2.33.11 has उपहत्नुम् (agent noun 'striker'); this text's उपहन्तुम् looks like an infinitive. The gloss treats it as an agent. Check the TS reading
TS reads आयेजे (perfect of आ+यज्); the text's आयजे may be a typo. Meaning 'won by worship' is fine
a11.salok 'ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ': Darpan glosses ਕਰਣ as ਜਗਤ/ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ (creation), ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ = the cause of creation; entry has 'करनेवाला/doer' (popular reading). Check Darpan before changing
a14.p3 'ਸੇ ਧਨਵੰਤ ਗਨੀ ਸੰਸਾਰ': may be Persian ਗਨੀ (ghani, rich) rather than 'counted' (Sant Singh: 'wealthy and prosperous'); site Hindi has 'गिने जाते हैं'. Possibly needs a second sense
a21.p7 'ਪਾਪੁ ਪੁੰਨੁ ਤਹ ਭਈ ਕਹਾਵਤ': feminine ਭਈ suggests ਕਹਾਵਤ is a fem. noun (talk/mention) rather than a present participle; g may be wrong
root 'ਉਪਾਰਜਣਾ' looks coined; Darpan relates ਉਪਰਜਾ to Skt उपार्जन (produced); a Sanskrit root (उप+अर्ज्) may be better

a13.p7 'ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਦੋਖਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ ਕੋਇ': both site translations say 'is satisfied', but the form may derive from Skt तिष्ठ- (stands, holds firm) as some teekas gloss it; no root given. Verify against Darpan
root ਪਰਾਨਣਾ is not a standard dictionary verb; sense 'recognizes, considers' (Darpan: ਪਛਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ) is right but the root needs checking
ਉਨ ਜਨ ਚਰਨ ਪਰਾਤਾ: may be 'has fallen (at the feet)' (past) rather than present 'पड़ता है'
Darpan may read ਪਾਸਾਰੀ as 'the one who spreads the show' rather than noun 'display'
root ਪੁੱਜਣਾ is doubtful: ਪੁਨੀ (ਇਛ ਪੁਨੀ 'wish fulfilled') is usually derived from पूर्ण (ਪੁੰਨਾ/ਪੁੰਨੀ = completed), not ਪੁੱਜਣਾ 'to reach'
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਦਰਸ ਪਿਆਸਾ may be adjective 'thirsty (for)' rather than noun 'thirst'; g says स्त्री॰ though form is -ਾ
ਹਉਮੈ ਬਿਖੁ ਫੈਲੁ: Darpan/Mahan Kosh may read ਫੈਲੁ as noun 'spread, ostentation' (or Persian fe'l 'deed'); entry gives adjective 'फैला हुआ' / 'all-consuming'
ਏਕ ਬਸਤੁ ਕਾਰਨਿ ਬਿਖੋਟਿ ਗਵਾਵੈ: hi 'विश्वास (खोकर)' mixes the verb ਗਵਾਵੈ into the gloss; Darpan reads ਬਿਖੋਟਿ roughly as 'by breach of faith / dishonesty'; needs a teeka check
root ਡੁੱਬਣਾ is the modern synonym; the Gurbani verb is ਬੂਡਣਾ/ਬੂਡਨਾ (Hindi बूड़ना); keep the glossary convention in mind before changing
ਜਨ ਕੈ ਬਿਰਤਿ ਬਿਬੇਕੈ: hi 'विवेककी, विवेकपूर्ण' (genitive/adjective) vs g संज्ञा; case of -ੈ here needs a teeka check
ਬੋਲਹਿ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖੀ: whether ਮੁਖੀ = 'chief, Supreme' (as entry) or 'with the mouth / turned towards' needs a teeka check
root ਲਹਿਣਾ (modern 'to come down/off') vs Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ 'to obtain' (< लभ्): same spelling in the glossary would mislead; consider a distinct root
root ਲਹਿਣਾ: the 'obtain' verb is Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ (< लभ्), distinct from modern ਲਹਿਣਾ 'come down'
root ਲਹਿਣਾ: the 'obtain/find' verb is Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ (< लभ्), distinct from modern ਲਹਿਣਾ 'come down'
ਜਿਸੁ ਧਨ ਤੇ ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਵਰਸਾਵੈ: hi mixes 'लाभ उठाता है' with 'बरसाता है' (rains); Darpan sense is 'is blessed/benefits'; 'बरसाता' likely wrong
ਜੈਸੇ ਸੂਰੁ ਸਰਬ ਕਉ ਸੋਖ: g 'संज्ञा' / hi 'सोखना' (infinitive) — here it functions verbally ('dries up / warms all'); grammar label needs a teeka check
aranya.17.cau10 सयन बुझाई: writer suggests adding 'सैन, इशारा' / 'sign, signal' to 'शयन, सोना'; no reviewer agreement in batch-03
aranya.18.cha1 कटि कसि निषंग: writer suggests 'कसकर' / 'having tightened, girding' (absolutive of कसना) beside 'कैसी, कैसे'; no reviewer agreement in batch-03

aranya.17.cau7: writer suggests vocative 'हे सुन्दरी' / 'O fair one' beside 'सुंदर स्त्रियाँ'; no reviewer agreement in batch-03
aranya.18.cau6 लै जानकिहि: writer suggests 'जानकीजीको' / object, not dative 'for'; g संप्रदान कारक may need to become कर्म; no reviewer agreement in batch-03
aranya.15.cau4: writer suggests general present 'देखता है' / 'sees' beside 'देखा'; no reviewer agreement in batch-03

aranya.43.cau2 कहउँ सहरोसा: entry has 'सहर्ष / प्रसन्नता से' (Gita Press: हर्षके साथ); writer and reviewer read स+रोष 'रोषसहित, ज़ोर देकर' / 'with vehemence, emphatically', which our meaning follows; readings differ, so the sense is unsettled
